requirements.GC-KIT-001: safety.viz's script-tag bundle is vendored as one file, `site/vendor/safety.viz/safety.viz.js`, with a source record beside it that names the safety.viz repository, the commit and version it was copied from, and the file's path there.
requirements.GC-KIT-002: The vendored bundle matches its recorded checksum and size. A bundle that is changed, missing, or beside a file the record does not name fails the check, and a second check fails when it differs from safety.viz's file at the recorded commit.
requirements.GC-KIT-003: The source record says whether the commit is on safety.viz's `dev` branch and, when it is not, says why and that the copy is to be made again from `dev`.
requirements.GC-KIT-004: The chart is built from `SafetyViz.kit`, found on the page: safety.viz's bundle and bio.viz's are two script tags, and every chart is drawn with the kit's Chart.js constructor.
requirements.GC-KIT-005: On a page without safety.viz the chart refuses to be made, with a message saying that `SafetyViz.kit` was not found.
requirements.GC-KIT-006: bio.viz's committed bundles contain none of safety.viz and no Chart.js: the build takes in only files under `src/`, the chart's source imports nothing from outside it, every file a committed bundle names as one it was made from is a file under `src/`, and the bundles hold no known marker of either library's code.
requirements.GC-CFG-001: Every setting has a default, and the column and baseline settings carry the core's names and defaults.
requirements.GC-CFG-002: A caller's settings are laid over the defaults; a column list is read the same whether written as names or as `{ value_col, label }`, and a single name the same as a list of one.
requirements.GC-CFG-003: A setting that is not known, or a value a setting cannot take, is refused with a message naming it.
requirements.GC-CFG-004: The chart has no setting that chooses a confidence level, a minimum group size or a cut, and none that adjusts the p-values of one test: the one setting that names an adjustment, `visit_adjustment`, names the one R is asked to make across the visits of one biomarker over time.
requirements.GC-CFG-005: The test and the pairwise comparisons each have a setting with a stated default: `test`, one of `t`, `wilcoxon`, `anova`, `kruskal` or `none`, default `t`, and `pairwise`, default false. `waiting_note` is a sentence a page adds to the waiting text. A value none can take is refused with a message naming it.
requirements.GC-BOX-001: A quantile is worked out by linear interpolation between the two nearest values at position (n − 1)p: R's `quantile(type = 7)`, the rule safety.viz's box plots use.
requirements.GC-BOX-002: On the synthetic study the count, the 5th, 25th, 50th, 75th and 95th percentiles, the least and greatest value and the mean of every box equal what desktop R gives for the same cell.
requirements.GC-VIOLIN-001: A violin's outline is a Gaussian kernel density of the cell's values at 64 heights from the least value to the greatest, with R's `bw.nrd0` as its smoothing width; on the synthetic study both equal what desktop R gives.
requirements.GC-VIOLIN-002: On a logarithmic axis a violin's outline is worked out on the base-10 logarithm of the values; a box is drawn from the values themselves on either axis.
requirements.GC-VIOLIN-003: A cell with one value, or with every value the same, has no outline; an outline is worked out only when violins are drawn.
requirements.GC-DATA-001: A panel holds one cell per level of the group, and each cell holds the participants the core's frame resolved at that level.
requirements.GC-DATA-002: The number of participants in each group is written beneath it, and with a colour the number in each colour.
requirements.GC-DATA-003: A second grouping by colour splits each level of the group into cells side by side that share the level's place on the axis.
requirements.GC-DATA-004: Panels by one further variable give one panel per level of it, and every panel is on the same value axis.
requirements.GC-DATA-005: With more than one visit chosen each visit is a panel, crossed with the panel variable when there is one; a baseline value has no visit.
requirements.GC-DATA-006: The levels chosen are the levels drawn: a level left out takes its participants with it.
requirements.GC-DATA-007: On a logarithmic axis a value of zero or less is left out and counted.
requirements.GC-DATA-008: A filter chooses participants: the ones filtered out are not drawn, and are not counted as missing a result.
requirements.GC-DATA-009: With the results table alone a group comes from a column carried on the results rows, and the cells are the ones the participant table would give.
requirements.GC-DATA-010: The value axis is named for the variable, with the unit its values are in; a fold change has no unit and a percent change is in percent.
requirements.GC-DATA-011: A point's place across its group's slot is fixed by the participant's id, so it does not move from one drawing to the next.
requirements.GC-DATA-012: The results-alone fixture is derived from the vendored study by a recorded rule: the results rows of two biomarkers, each with the participant's `ARM` added. Deriving it again gives the committed file.
requirements.GC-DATA-013: With no column to group by, everyone is drawn as one group.
requirements.GC-CTRL-001: With participant data, the columns offered to group, colour and panel by are the participant table's categories: its columns with at most `max_levels` different values, other than the id.
requirements.GC-CTRL-002: With the results table alone, the columns offered are the ones carried on its rows that are not mapped by a setting and hold one value for each participant.
requirements.GC-CTRL-003: Filters are the participant table's categories, or the columns named in settings that the participant table has; without a participant table there are none.
requirements.GC-CTRL-004: The biomarkers, the visits in visit order and the visits the chart opens on, every one of them unless the settings name some, are read from the results table.
requirements.GC-CTRL-005: The biomarker, the value type and the visit are chosen in the sidebar, and the chart follows; a baseline value has no Visit control.
requirements.GC-CTRL-006: The levels of the group are chosen in the sidebar, and a level left out is not drawn.
requirements.GC-CTRL-007: Reset chart returns every control and filter to what the chart opened on.
requirements.GC-DRAW-001: The chart draws a box per group with safety.viz's box drawing, with the number in each group beneath, and the quartiles on the page are the ones desktop R gives.
requirements.GC-DRAW-002: The chart draws a violin per group, by a plugin on the kit's Chart.js.
requirements.GC-DRAW-003: The chart draws points, one per participant, each at its value and within its group's place.
requirements.GC-DRAW-004: A second grouping by colour is drawn side by side with a legend and the count in each colour.
requirements.GC-DRAW-005: Panels by one further variable, and by visit, are each a chart of their own on one value axis.
requirements.GC-DRAW-006: The value axis can be logarithmic; values of zero or less are left out and the note above the chart counts them.
requirements.GC-FILTER-001: Loaded with the results table alone the chart draws and shows no filters, and a group comes from a column carried on the results rows.
requirements.GC-FILTER-002: Loaded with the synthetic results as vendored, which carry no group column, the chart says that no column can make a group and draws everyone as one group, with no filters.
requirements.GC-FILTER-003: Loaded with participant data the chart shows a filter per category column and offers the participant-level variables to group, colour and panel by.
requirements.GC-FILTER-004: A filter narrows the participants drawn, and the counts beneath the groups and the note above the chart follow.
requirements.GC-FILTER-005: When the filters together let no participant through, the chart hands the core no results table of no rows, which the core refuses as malformed: one biomarker and the overview have no panels and say that nobody passed. With no kit on the page an empty selection is not a filter in force and lets everyone through.
requirements.GC-FILTER-006: On the demo, filters with nobody in common leave the overview and one biomarker reading `No participant passes the filters.`, with the note that none of the participants pass; nothing is drawn, R is asked nothing, the filters and Reset chart stay usable, nothing is written to the console, and loosening a filter draws again.
requirements.GC-FILTER-007: A filter reads its spec by the rule safety.viz's charts follow, through the kit's `reconcileFilters`: `start` sets what it opens on and All is still offered; only `all: false` removes All, and its first value is then the one in force; a value the data lacks falls back to All with a console warning naming the filter; and the selection each control shows is the selection the chart filters by.
requirements.GC-LIST-001: Clicking a box lists its participants in the kit's record listing, whose search and paging work on them.
requirements.GC-LIST-002: A change to a control or a filter empties the listing, so it never lists a box that is no longer drawn.
requirements.GC-LIST-003: The listing's export downloads the listed rows as CSV under this chart's name.
requirements.GC-LIST-004: Clicking a point lists its participant and opens their profile.
requirements.GC-PROF-001: A row of the listing selects its participant: the chart raises safety.viz's `participantsSelected` event with the participant's id, and safety.viz's participant profile opens on it with the participant's own columns and biomarkers. Clearing the profile clears the selection.
requirements.GC-STAT-001: With no R attached the statistics line reads exactly what the connection answers.
requirements.GC-STAT-002: From the moment a result is asked for until it arrives, the line says it is waiting; the answer is printed through the shared formatter.
requirements.GC-STAT-003: R is asked with the rows that were drawn and the names of their fields.
requirements.GC-STAT-004: An answer that arrives after the chart has been drawn again is never shown.
requirements.GC-STAT-005: What R declined to compute, what the formatter refuses, and what R reports as an error are each printed as such.
requirements.GC-STAT-006: On the page, with no R attached, the statistics line of every panel reads that statistics are unavailable, and nothing is fetched to say so.
requirements.GC-STAT-007: On the page, with a connection given in settings, the line shows that it is waiting until R answers and then prints the answer; R is asked for the rows that are drawn.
requirements.GC-STAT-008: On the page, a filter change clears the line before asking again, and an answer for the rows before the change is never shown.
requirements.GC-STAT-009: The tests offered are the ones that fit the number of groups drawn: a Welch t-test or a Wilcoxon rank-sum test for two, a one-way ANOVA or a Kruskal-Wallis test for more, and none for fewer than two. A test that does not fit gives way to its counterpart of the same kind, means with means and ranks with ranks, so R is never sent a test it would refuse for the number of groups.
requirements.GC-STAT-010: What R is asked for a panel is the function named in settings, the panel's rows, and four arguments: `strValueCol`, `strGroupCol`, `strMethod` and `bPairwise`. Pairwise comparisons are asked for only when the switch is on and the rows hold more than two groups. Nothing else is sent: the adjustment, the confidence level and the minimum group size are R's defaults.
requirements.GC-STAT-011: The identity of a panel's rows states what was drawn by the settings' names: the biomarker, the value type, the visit, the baseline settings, the group column, the groups in the rows, the colour column, the panel, the filters in force, and whether zero or less was left out. A member that is not set is left out, lists are sorted by code point, and a change to anything that changes the rows changes the identity.
requirements.GC-STAT-012: The result is printed through the shared formatter with its method and counts, labelled exploratory and unadjusted, for each of the four tests, with no star and never the word significant.
requirements.GC-STAT-013: For two groups the difference in means is printed with its interval, from R's `estimates`, with what it is the difference of. With more than two groups R gives none and none is printed.
requirements.GC-STAT-014: Pairwise comparisons are printed as a table of each pair, its two counts and its adjusted p-value, under a caption that names the method and labels them adjusted, by the name of the adjustment R used. Where R used more than one method among the pairs each pair names its own, and a pair R could not compute says why.
requirements.GC-STAT-015: R's warnings and notes are printed with the result, as R worded them.
requirements.GC-STAT-016: A group below the minimum size prints R's reason once and no number, and a result R marked as an error prints R's message.
requirements.GC-STAT-017: With fewer than two groups to compare, in the chart or in one panel, the line says that a test compares two or more groups, and what was found.
requirements.GC-STAT-018: What one test covers is said under it: the participants drawn in that panel, that each panel has a test of its own and they are not adjusted for one another, that a second grouping by colour is not part of it, and the filters in force.
requirements.GC-STAT-019: The waiting text carries the page's note on what starting R costs until R has answered once, and not after.
requirements.GC-STAT-020: A view with no stored result reads that statistics are unavailable for this view, in the chart's own words.
requirements.GC-STAT-021: The rows desktop R is run on are the chart's: each case is one panel of the gallery's demo in one view, its rows made by the chart's own code from the demo's own tables and settings, and deriving them again gives the committed files.
requirements.GC-STAT-022: The expected results name the script, the R version, and the commit and checksum of the vendored statistics file that made them, and hold one result per case: the four tests, the pairwise comparisons and a group below the minimum size among them.
requirements.GC-STAT-023: A stored result written from R by the documented recipe is one the chart finds: for every case the function, the arguments, the identity and the row count R wrote are the ones the chart asks with, and handed to a connection each answer is found by its panel's request and by no other view's.
requirements.GC-STAT-024: gsm.bio's statistics file is vendored as one file, `site/vendor/gsm.bio/statistics.R`, with a source record beside it naming the gsm.bio repository, the commit and the file's path there. It defines the function the chart asks for, attaches no package, and names the survival package only inside its survival functions.
requirements.GC-STAT-025: The vendored statistics file matches its recorded checksum and size. A file that is edited, missing, or beside a file the record does not name fails the check, and a second check fails when it differs from gsm.bio's file at the recorded commit.
requirements.GC-STAT-026: On the page, the Test control offers only the tests that fit the number of groups drawn, and the pairwise switch is there only with more than two groups; R is sent only a test the control offered.
requirements.GC-STAT-027: On the page, with one group drawn, with no column to group by, with one group in a panel, or with no test chosen, R is not asked, and the line says why.
requirements.GC-STAT-028: On the page, a change to the test, the pairwise switch, a filter or a variable each clears the line and asks R again for what is then drawn, and the answer to the question before is never shown.
requirements.GC-STAT-029: On the page, each panel asks R for itself, on its own rows and under its own identity, and is answered for itself: one biomarker at two visits is two requests, and one panel prints while the other still waits.
requirements.GC-STAT-030: On the page, with R's answers stored and no R attached, a view an answer was stored for prints it with no request to R's hosts, each panel from its own stored result, and a view none was stored for reads unavailable, never another view's numbers.
requirements.GC-STAT-031: On the page, the line prints what R returned: the result, the difference in means, the pairwise table, R's warnings and notes, and R's reason for a group too small.
requirements.GC-STAT-032: At a 390-pixel-wide viewport the chart with a pairwise table under it holds, and the page does not scroll sideways.
requirements.GC-STAT-033: With R attached and no test chosen the page fetches nothing for R; the first test chosen starts R and fetches its file of functions, once.
requirements.GC-STAT-034: The gallery's demo draws first and starts R in the browser when its first panel asks for a test, from webR's pinned version and gsm.bio's vendored statistics file, with no R package installed. The line waits, saying what the first start costs, and then prints the Welch t-test, which equals desktop R's for the same rows within 1 part in 10^8.
requirements.GC-STAT-035: On the demo, the Wilcoxon rank-sum test equals desktop R's for the same rows, and R is not started again.
requirements.GC-STAT-036: On the demo, with four groups, the one-way ANOVA equals desktop R's for the same rows.
requirements.GC-STAT-037: On the demo, the Kruskal-Wallis test equals desktop R's for the same rows.
requirements.GC-STAT-038: On the demo, the pairwise comparisons, adjusted by Holm, equal desktop R's. Where R's own answer differs between the desktop's version and the browser's, `wilcox.test` with ties in groups of fewer than 50, both answers are recorded side by side, the difference is confirmed to be that case, and every other number is still held equal.
requirements.GC-STAT-039: On the demo, a filter change shows the waiting state and then the new result, which equals desktop R's, and never the old one.
requirements.GC-STAT-040: On the demo, a group below the minimum size prints R's reason, once, and no number.
requirements.GC-STAT-041: The megabytes and seconds of the demo's first test are measured, printed in the run's log and written to a file with both versions' answers, and are what the page tells its reader in the waiting text.
requirements.GC-STAT-042: On a phone the demo prints R's result and a pairwise table, and the page does not scroll sideways.
requirements.GC-OVW-001: With no visit named in settings the chart opens on every visit it draws, in visit order; visits that are named are the ones it opens on, as before. With no biomarker named it opens on none alone. Both settings default to null.
requirements.GC-OVW-002: `overview_limit` and `page`, the settings of the overview v0.2.0 drew a page at a time, are still settings, checked as they were: a whole number of one or more, twelve by default, and a whole number from nought. Neither is applied to the trend tiles, which draw every biomarker.
requirements.GC-OVW-006: The group, the levels, the value, the scale, the visits and the filters apply to every tile. A second grouping by colour, panels by a further variable and the mark are not applied there: the tiles are the same with each set as without. With no column to group by everyone is one line, and a cut variable makes the same groups in every tile.
requirements.GC-OVW-007: A baseline value has no visit. For a change, a fold change or a percent change from baseline, the one baseline visit is not drawn as a panel of one biomarker’s view: there the value is the same for every participant. With several baseline visits every visit is drawn.
requirements.GC-OVW-009: The levels the tiles offer are the group column’s own, read from the table that holds it.
requirements.GC-OVW-010: The many-biomarkers fixture is derived from the vendored study by a recorded rule: the results of the first forty participants at two visits, written three times, twice with a letter added to each biomarker’s name, which makes thirty-six biomarkers. Deriving it again gives the committed file.
requirements.GC-OVW-011: On the page, with no biomarker named, the chart opens on the trend tiles: the Biomarker control reads All Biomarkers and the Visit control all visits; the twelve biomarkers of the synthetic study each have one tile, in the control’s order, drawn with the kit’s Chart.js, with a line per group in the groups’ colours across the five visits, the first and last visit named and the axis’s range and unit printed beneath, and one key above all the tiles; there is no statistics line and nothing leads to further pages.
requirements.GC-OVW-012: A tile is a button named for its biomarker, with its range read out with it, that opens the biomarker over time, by a click or by Enter or Space: across its visits in one picture, with a row of tests under them. All Biomarkers in the control returns to the tiles, Reset returns to what the settings open on, and a setting that names a biomarker opens it.
requirements.GC-OVW-013: The tiles ask R for nothing, with R attached and R’s hosts in reach: no call, no request to R’s hosts, no waiting text and an empty `chart.statistics()`, however they are redrawn. Opening a biomarker asks once, for the row of its visits, with the key desktop R wrote for the same view; the row waits while the page goes on answering clicks, and an answer that arrives after a visit was opened, or after the tiles are back, is dropped.
requirements.GC-OVW-014: On the page Group by, Levels, Value, Scale, Visit and the filters apply to every tile. Colour by, Panel by and Draw as are switched off there, each with words saying where it applies, and keep what they are set to: Draw as is a control again once a biomarker is open, and Colour by and Panel by once a biomarker and a visit are. There is no Statistics section on the tiles.
requirements.GC-OVW-015: With thirty-six biomarkers every one has a tile: there are no pages and no count of how many are shown, and `overview_limit` and `page`, still read and kept by a specification, change nothing.
requirements.GC-OVW-016: At a 390-pixel-wide viewport the tiles are two to a line, each whole with its chart inside it and its range on one line beneath, a tap on a tile opens the biomarker over time at the chart’s top, the note of unscheduled visits left out holds too, and the page does not scroll sideways.
requirements.GC-OVW-017: The first draw of thirty-six tiles, a Chart.js chart each, is timed at a desk’s width and at a phone’s, printed in the run’s log and written to a file, and stays under a generous bound.
requirements.GC-OVW-018: The gallery’s demo opens on the trend tiles, one per biomarker of the synthetic study with a line per arm and R’s medians, with neither a biomarker nor a visit named and no statistics line, and fetches nothing for R, with R’s hosts in reach, until a biomarker is opened. The study has no unscheduled visit, so the demo shows neither the note nor the control.
requirements.GC-OVW-019: On the demo, with real R in the browser, the tiles start no R; opening a biomarker starts it once; the row of tests under its visits waits, saying what the first start costs, and then prints under every visit the p-value desktop R gives, unadjusted and, once the switch is set, adjusted, each from one request whose answer equals desktop R’s for the same rows within 1 part in 10^8; a few of its visits, a panel each, each wait and print the test desktop R gives for that visit; and returning to the tiles and opening another biomarker fetches nothing more.
requirements.GC-LIFE-001: `init`, `setData`, `setSettings`, `render`, `resize` and `destroy` drive the chart as they drive a safety.viz chart.
requirements.GC-LIFE-002: Tables the chart cannot read are refused with a message, shown in the chart's element.
requirements.GC-LIFE-003: The chart can be mounted inside another chart's element on one biomarker, with a way back: the setting `back` puts a button above the chart that calls the caller's function with the chart, by a click or from the keyboard; without it there is no button.
requirements.GC-MOBILE-001: At a 390-pixel-wide viewport the chart fills the width with its controls folded away one tap from open, panels stack one to a row, and the page does not scroll sideways.
requirements.GC-MOBILE-002: At a 390-pixel-wide viewport a box can be tapped, its listing read and a profile opened below the chart, and the page still does not scroll sideways.
requirements.GC-SITE-001: The gallery lists the group comparison chart with its picture and links to its live demo, its evidence page and its API reference.
requirements.GC-SITE-002: The live demo draws the chart on the synthetic study from safety.viz's vendored bundle and bio.viz's committed one, with R attached and gsm.bio's statistics file published beside it. Where R's host cannot be reached it still draws, and its statistics line says that R could not be started.
requirements.GC-SITE-003: The live demo holds at a 390-pixel-wide viewport with no horizontal scroll.
requirements.GC-SITE-004: The API reference has a table row for every setting the chart has; the site build fails when one is missing.
requirements.GC-STAT-043: When the connection is replaced (`setSettings({ connection })`), an answer that arrives late from the connection it replaced is never shown: it changes neither the statistics line nor what `chart.statistics()` reports.
requirements.GC-FAIL-001: When drawing fails, the group comparison says so in its footnote (`This chart could not be drawn:` and why), takes away what was drawn of the panels, ends the statistics round, empties the listing and the participant rail, says it in the danger colour and keeps its controls; once drawing works again it draws.
requirements.GC-DROP-001: With a participant table, a participant the results have and the table does not is left out and counted (`Not in the participant table`), and a row of results with no participant id is counted (`Row has no participant id`); a participant table without the participant id column is refused with a sentence that names the column.
requirements.GC-STAT-044: A stored result written by the R recipe from a data frame whose panel column holds numbers is found by the chart: the recipe writes the panel, the measure, the visits, the groups and the filters as text, as the chart does (`chart_text`).
requirements.GC-DROP-002: With results for participants the participant table does not have and filters that let nobody through, the chart says `No participant passes the filters.`, as it does with no such rows.
requirements.GC-DROP-003: A setting that names a participant id column the participant table does not have (`setSettings({ participant_id_col })`) is refused with the same sentence as the tables are, before anything changes, and the chart stays as it was drawn.
requirements.GC-STAT-045: The recipes' `chart_text` writes each value as the chart's `String()` does: logicals as `true` and `false`, numbers in the fewest digits that read back the same, in full from 1e-6 to below 1e21 and with an exponent outside that.
requirements.GC-FAIL-002: A failure while the controls are built, where the Levels control reads the groups, is said like any other: the footnote says the chart could not be drawn, and nothing is thrown.
requirements.GC-DRAW-007: With one biomarker open at several visits, the groups' labels under each visit's panel do not run into one another, at 1280 and at 390 pixels wide: they stay level when they fit and turn when they would not.
requirements.GC-CTRL-008: With one biomarker open, the Visit control offers, and the chart draws, only the visits that biomarker has values at, in visit order; the overview offers every visit.
requirements.GC-DROP-004: The participant table and the setting that names its id column change together: `setData(tables, settings)` checks the tables against the settings it is given with them, lays the settings over, and draws.
requirements.GC-OVW-020: Every visit chosen keeps its place along every tile, so the tiles line up. Where a group has no value at a visit it has no point there, and its line runs on to its next value; a biomarker with no value to draw has a tile with no axis.
requirements.GC-DRAW-008: With five long arm names, the groups' labels under each visit's panel do not run into one another at 1280 pixels wide.
requirements.GC-STAT-046: The recipes' `chart_text` writes NaN as `NaN`, and holds to the chart's `String()` for numbers of 13 significant digits, the most its claim covers.
requirements.GC-STAT-047: An estimate R gave a bound for but no number, or half an interval, is said not to be shown, and why; it never vanishes, while the means R gives no interval for are left out.
requirements.GC-CUT-001: The chart draws a biomarker by a cut biomarker as its category: IL-6's change to Week 4 by CRP at Baseline cut at the median, the tertiles, the quartiles and typed points, on the synthetic study, the groups low to high with the number in each beneath, each participant in the group desktop R puts them in.
requirements.GC-CUT-002: With a cut category or panel the footnote states the cut and its points, and how many participants' values they were worked out on.
requirements.GC-CUT-003: A cut biomarker can make the panels, in its order low to high, each panel holding the participants desktop R puts in that group.
requirements.GC-CUT-004: When repeated cut points collapse, or points written alike merge groups, the footnote says so and how many groups they make instead; a cut variable with no value says it makes no groups.
requirements.GC-CUT-005: `group_by` and `panel_by` take a column or a cut variable, which the settings keep as the core writes one; a variable with no cut, or a malformed cut, is refused with a sentence, and so is a cut of a biomarker or a column the tables do not have; `color_by` stays a column.
requirements.GC-CUT-006: A cut's points are worked out on the participants the filters keep who have a value of the cut variable, whether or not they have a value to draw, so a visit's panels share one set of groups; they move when the filters do.
requirements.GC-CUT-007: The statistics request names a cut category in the identity of its rows as the cut variable written by the settings' own names, and the groups by their labels, so a stored result written from R is found.
requirements.GC-CUT-008: A cut category has no Levels control: every group it makes is drawn, and the controls say so.
requirements.GC-CUT-009: R is handed a cut category's groups low to high (`chrGroups`), so its result names them in the order they are drawn and a difference in means is of the lower minus the higher; the identity of the rows keeps them sorted by code point, and a column's groups are not named, so v0.1.0's keys are unchanged.
requirements.GC-CUT-010: With R's stored answers for cut groups, the statistics line names the groups low to high, and a group below R's minimum size prints R's reason and counts, as R worded them.
requirements.GC-LVL-001: Which level is drawn is decided in one place from what the controls are set to: with no biomarker chosen, every biomarker; with one chosen and every visit it has, that biomarker over time; with one chosen and some of its visits, those visits, a panel each.
requirements.GC-LVL-002: A biomarker with values at one visit only, and a baseline value, which has no visit, have no picture over time: with every visit chosen they are drawn as the single view.
requirements.GC-TIME-001: One biomarker over time has three settings: `time_mark`, what the picture is drawn as, `box`, `mean_se` or `median_iqr`, `box` by default; `visit_adjustment`, the adjustment of the p-values across the visits by the name R’s `p.adjust()` gives it, `none`, `holm` or `BH`, `none` by default; and `statistic_by_visit`, the R function that answers a row of visits, `Analyze_GroupDifferenceBy` by default, or null for no row of tests. A value none can take is refused with a message naming it.
requirements.GC-TIME-002: The picture has one column per visit the biomarker has values at, in visit order, and in each a cell per group drawn, side by side in the group’s order and colour, which a group keeps at every visit. A second grouping by colour and panels are not applied, whatever those controls hold.
requirements.GC-TIME-003: A cell describes the records the single-visit view draws for that group at that visit, one per participant from the core’s frame: nothing is pooled across visits.
requirements.GC-TIME-004: On the synthetic study every cell’s count, quantiles, mean, standard deviation and standard error, by arm at every visit, for the result and for the change from baseline, equal what desktop R gives: `length()`, `quantile(type = 7)`, `mean()`, `sd()` and `sd() / sqrt(n)`.
requirements.GC-TIME-005: Each form is drawn from the cell’s own numbers: a box from its quartiles, with a line at the median and whiskers at the 5th and 95th percentiles; a mean with one standard error either side; a median with the 25th and 75th percentiles either side. A group of one has a mean and no standard error.
requirements.GC-TIME-006: The value axis covers what the form draws, with a little room at each end: the whiskers’ ends for boxes, the standard errors’ for means, the quartiles for medians. On a logarithmic axis the room is a ratio and the lower end stays above zero.
requirements.GC-TIME-007: For a change, a fold change or a percent change from one baseline visit, that visit is drawn, where every group starts at no change, and is not tested: it is not among the visits R is asked about. With several baseline visits, and for the result itself, every visit is tested.
requirements.GC-TIME-008: R is asked once for the whole row of visits. The request holds the rows of every visit tested, one per participant and visit, each the row its own panel would hand R with the visit named; its arguments name the value, the group and the visit columns, the test, the visits in visit order (`chrBy`) and the adjustment by R’s name for it (`strPAdjust`).
requirements.GC-TIME-009: The identity of the rows names the chart, the biomarker, the value, the visits tested in visit order, the baseline visits and how they are combined, the grouping variable, the groups sorted by code point, the filters in force and a logarithmic axis that left values out; it has no colour and no panel member, whatever those controls hold, and says `unscheduled_visits: true` only when unscheduled visits are drawn and the results have some.
requirements.GC-TIME-010: The baseline visit of a change is not sent: R is asked about the later visits alone, on their rows alone, so it is never asked to test a value that is the same for everyone.
requirements.GC-TIME-011: A cut’s groups are handed to R low to high (`chrGroups`), as for one panel, so R names them in the order they are drawn at every visit; a column’s groups are not named, and R takes the groups in the rows. The identity names the cut variable and keeps the groups sorted by code point.
requirements.GC-TIME-012: The rows desktop R is run on for one biomarker over time are derived with the chart’s own code from the demo’s own tables and settings, a file per view, with a table of the cases; deriving them again gives the committed files.
requirements.GC-TIME-013: For every case the function, the arguments, the identity and the row count desktop R wrote by the recipe are the ones the chart asks with, and handed to a connection as stored results each answer is found by the chart’s request and by no other view’s.
requirements.GC-TIME-014: Each visit’s p-value in R’s one answer is the one R gives when that visit is asked about alone, and the adjusted one is what R’s `p.adjust()` makes of those across the visits that have one.
requirements.GC-TIME-015: Each visit’s result is read from R’s row for it, in parts: its p-value as R returned it, adjusted where R adjusted, with the method and each group’s count; and the line under the table names the method once, how many visits were tested, and the adjustment R made with how many visits it covered.
requirements.GC-TIME-016: When no visit could be tested the line gives R’s reason for the whole request once and each visit’s beneath; where the visits’ tests differ in name each visit’s sentence is given; and an answer that is not a row of visits, no R and an R error are each said as such, with no number.
requirements.GC-TIME-017: The statistics desk asks once for the row of visits, says that it is waiting until R answers, reads the answer as a row of results, and drops an answer that arrives after the chart was drawn again.
requirements.GC-TIME-018: What the tests cover is said in plain words under them: a test of its own at each visit, of the levels of the grouping variable on the participants drawn at that visit; the baseline visit of a change that is not tested, and why; and the filters in force.
requirements.GC-TIME-019: On the page, a biomarker opened from its tile is drawn across its visits in one picture, on the kit’s Chart.js: visit along the bottom in visit order, the groups side by side in their colours as safety.viz’s boxes, each visit named under its place, and under each visit the number in each group. The boxes and the counts are desktop R’s; a key says what is drawn, a caption how a box is read, and the picture is named for a reader who cannot see it.
requirements.GC-TIME-020: Drawn as means with standard errors, each group is a point at desktop R’s mean at each visit with a bar one standard error either side, joined across the visits by a line in the group’s colour; the key and the caption say so, and the value axis is the bars’.
requirements.GC-TIME-021: Drawn as medians with quartiles, each group is a point at desktop R’s median with a bar from the 25th to the 75th percentile, joined by a line. `time_mark` opens the chart on a form, the Draw as control reads it and keeps it from one biomarker to the next, and for a change from baseline every group starts at nought at the baseline visit.
requirements.GC-TIME-022: Under each visit the row of tests prints the p-value desktop R returns for that visit, by the shared rule, from one request for the whole row, with the whole sentence in the cell’s title. The Adjust across visits switch asks R again, with the adjustment by its `p.adjust()` name, and prints R’s adjusted p-values in their place; the row’s heading and the line under the table name the adjustment R made and how many visits it covered. Where the p-values are not small the two readings differ in print, and each is R’s.
requirements.GC-TIME-023: The row of tests says that it is waiting until R answers, with the picture and the counts already drawn, and then prints each visit’s p-value and the adjustment R names. A change to the test, the adjustment or a filter clears the row and asks again, in one request, and the answer to the question before is never shown.
requirements.GC-TIME-024: On the page, for a change from baseline the baseline visit is drawn, every group at nought, and is not tested: its name is not a button, its cell reads not tested, its rows are not sent to R, a click in its part of the picture opens nothing, and the notes and the line under the table say why. The adjustment is across the visits tested.
requirements.GC-TIME-025: With no R attached the picture and the counts are drawn all the same, the row of tests says that statistics are unavailable, the line under the table says so in full, and nothing is fetched. With no test chosen, or with one group drawn, R is not asked and the row says so.
requirements.GC-TIME-026: A visit’s name in the table is a button, named for the biomarker and the visit, that opens that visit alone, by a click or by the keyboard: the single-visit view as released, with its own question for R under the key it always had, and the keyboard’s place on the Visit control. A trail above the chart names the level drawn and leads back to the biomarker over time and to every biomarker, as All in the Visit control and All Biomarkers do; some of the visits, not all, are a panel each.
requirements.GC-TIME-027: Over time, Colour by and Panel by are switched off, each with words saying that it applies once a biomarker and a visit are open; Draw as offers the three forms; and Statistics offers the test that fits the number of groups and the adjustment across visits, and no pairwise switch. Group by, Levels, Value, Scale and the filters apply to the picture and its table. A baseline value is drawn as the single view.
requirements.GC-TIME-028: A visit R did not compute, because a group there has fewer than R’s minimum or nobody, reads not computed in its cell, with R’s reason and R’s counts in the cell’s title and under the table, and the picture and the counts still show the group. R’s adjustment is across the visits that have a p-value, and the line says how many. When R computes none, every cell says so and the line gives R’s reason. At a visit where a group has nobody, R still answers for every group and says which has none: the group keeps its row of counts, with a count of nought, and its colour, and has no mark there.
requirements.GC-TIME-029: With more than two groups the row of tests is the several-group test desktop R returns at each visit, a one-way ANOVA or a Kruskal-Wallis test, adjusted across the visits when asked, with each group’s count in the cell’s title.
requirements.GC-TIME-030: Over time the PNG holds the picture with its table of counts and tests, the statistics file holds R’s result and R’s row for every visit, the table file holds a row per participant and visit drawn, the title, the subtitle and the chart’s own footnote are filled from the level drawn, and the specification written, with the form and the adjustment, makes the same picture again.
requirements.GC-TIME-031: At a 390-pixel-wide viewport the picture over time and its table hold five visits within the page, with every cell of the row of tests inside it; a tap on a visit opens it at the chart’s top; and with more visits than fit, the picture and the table scroll sideways together inside the chart and the page does not.
requirements.GC-TIME-032: A specification written by bio.viz v0.2.0 that names a biomarker and every visit, which drew a panel for every visit, is read whole and now opens on the biomarker over time: the same participants at each visit in the same groups, one request where there were five, and one click from the released view of any of its visits, asked of R under the released key. Written again it holds every setting the released one held.
requirements.GC-TILE-001: There is one tile per biomarker, in the Biomarker control’s order, named for it, with the unit of its values; in each, one line per group, with a point at each visit chosen, in visit order. A fold change has no unit and a percent change is in percent.
requirements.GC-TILE-002: A point describes the records that biomarker’s own view draws for that group at that visit, one per participant from the core’s frame: how many, their median and their mean. The point is drawn at the median, or at the mean when the tiles are switched to means. Nothing is pooled across visits or across biomarkers.
requirements.GC-TILE-003: On the synthetic study every tile’s medians, means and counts, by arm at every visit, for the result and for the change from baseline, equal what desktop R gives: `median()`, `mean()` and `length()`.
requirements.GC-TILE-004: Each biomarker has its own value axis: from the least point drawn to the greatest, widened about its middle until it spans `tile_min_spread` times the standard deviation of the results at the baseline visit, with a tenth of its span as room at each end; its two ends, to the figures its span calls for, and its unit are what is printed under the tile. The standard deviation is of each participant’s baseline value among the participants drawn, and on the synthetic study it equals desktop R’s `sd()`.
requirements.GC-TILE-005: The least an axis spans is in the units of what the tile draws: the standard deviation itself for a result, a baseline value or a change; over the mean of the baseline values for a fold change, and a hundred times that for a percent change; and on a logarithmic scale a ratio, ten to the power of the standard deviation of the base-10 logarithms, for a result, a baseline value or a fold change. A change or a percent change on a logarithmic scale has none, and neither has a tile with fewer than two baseline values: its axis is left at its points. An axis of results none of which is negative is not widened below zero.
requirements.GC-TILE-006: The tiles have two settings: `tile_summary`, `median` or `mean`, `median` by default, and `tile_min_spread`, a number of zero or more, 1.25 by default, where zero means no least. A value neither can take is refused with a message naming it.
requirements.GC-TILE-007: For a change, a fold change or a percent change from baseline a tile keeps the baseline visit, where every line starts at no change, and marks where no change is. A baseline value has no visit, so each group is one point.
requirements.GC-TILE-008: On the page each tile’s line goes through the medians desktop R gives for that arm at each visit, for the result and for the change from baseline, and through R’s means when the Tiles draw control, or `tile_summary`, is set to means; the key above the tiles says which. The control is there only on the tiles.
requirements.GC-TILE-009: On the page a tile’s value axis never spans less than `tile_min_spread` times desktop R’s standard deviation of the results at the baseline visit, the range printed under the tile is the axis’s own two ends, a sentence above the tiles says what the least is, and the multiple is a setting; on a logarithmic scale the axis is logarithmic and its ends are at least that ratio apart.
requirements.GC-TILE-010: A specification written by the released chart, bio.viz v0.2.0, is still read, validates against the schema, and rebuilds its view: one visit, or a panel per visit, with the panels, the groups and the questions for R the released chart had, key for key; and the overview it drew a page at a time as a tile for every biomarker. Written again it holds every setting the released one held. A specification this version writes holds the tiles’ settings and the rule for unscheduled visits, and makes the same tiles again. The one view that is not rebuilt as it was is a biomarker at every visit (GC-TIME-032).
requirements.GC-UNS-001: The chart has safety.viz’s three settings of unscheduled visits, under safety.viz’s names and with the defaults of its results over time chart: `unscheduled_visits`, false; `unscheduled_visit_pattern`, `/unscheduled
requirements.GC-UNS-002: With unscheduled visits left out, the results at them are set aside before anything is listed or framed: such a visit is in no tile and is not a panel of one biomarker, and with no baseline visit named the baseline is the first scheduled visit. What R is asked for a scheduled visit is what it is asked of a table without those rows, and the identity of the rows says `unscheduled_visits: true` only when they are drawn and the results have some; a key R writes by the recipe for such a view is the chart’s.
requirements.GC-UNS-003: On the page, with rows for unscheduled visits added to the study, such a visit is in no tile, not in the Visit control, not a visit of a biomarker over time and not a panel of one, and a note above the chart says how many are left out and which. The Unscheduled visits control, or `unscheduled_visits`, brings them in at every level, in visit order, and the one request for a biomarker over time then names them among its visits and says that the rows hold unscheduled visits; the control is there only when the results have such a visit; and a specification keeps the switch.
requirements.GC-UNS-004: On the page a list of names in `unscheduled_visit_values` decides alone which visits are unscheduled, whatever the pattern says; a list of none means no visit; another pattern names others; the note counts and names what is left out; and a pattern that is no regular expression is refused by name with nothing changed.
requirements.GC-UNS-005: On the page, an unscheduled visit that is left out is not the baseline a change is measured from: with no baseline visit named it is the first scheduled visit, and R is asked what it is asked of the study without that visit. Switched on, the first visit of all is the baseline, and the identity of the rows says that they hold unscheduled visits.
requirements.GC-UNS-006: A specification that names an unscheduled visit while they are left out, as one written by v0.2.0 for a study that has them does, is read, and the visit is left out like any other: the notice above the chart names the visits and the setting that would draw them, and does not say that they are missing from the tables. With `unscheduled_visits` true in the specification the visits are drawn and nothing is said.
